candidates.title: Naïve Autonomous Company Hackathon: Build an agent-run company that runs itself
candidates.evidence:
Hosted By
Y Combinator
Naïve Autonomous Company Hackathon
Saturday, November 7
San Francisco, CA
Capacity 200
About Event
A two-day hackathon for builders who want to start a company run by agents.

Join Naïve at the YC office in San Francisco. Choose a business, build its team with the Naïve SDK, and put it to work: finding customers, delivering the product, and running day-to-day operations.

At demo time, show the company operating. Not just what it could do, but what its agents actually accomplished. What did they deliver? What decisions did they make? Where did you need to step in?

Applications are reviewed by Naïve and YC, and attendance is subject to approval.

### About Naïve

Naïve is building autonomous companies: agent systems that can run real businesses end to end.

Use the Naïve SDK to create the agents that run your company, connect their tools, set their budgets, and keep their work running. Our studio lets you deploy and operate these systems.

We've raised a $28.5M Series A from Nexus Venture Partners, Y Combinator, Zetta Venture Partners, Liquid 2, and leading operators.

### What You Can Build

Build any company that is primarily run by agents. The industry and business model are up to you.

All teams must use the Naïve SDK to build their company. SDK documentation: [usenaive.ai/docs](https://usenaive.ai/docs)

A few examples (not required tracks):

 Media companies: Agents decide what to publish, produce the content, and use audience results to plan what comes next.
 Agencies: Agents find prospects, scope projects, deliver client work, and manage follow-up.
 Commerce businesses: Agents choose what to sell, run campaigns, handle customer requests, and adjust based on sales.
 Software businesses: Agents build a product, bring in users, handle support, and decide what to improve from customer feedback.

### Prizes

We'll recognize 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place overall, plus winners in these categories:

 Most Likely to Become a Unicorn
 People's Choice
 Best Mobile Automation

Prizes
\- iPhone 18 pro / airpods 5 AND a guaranteed YC interview for 1st place

\- $50,000+ in sponsor credits for 1st place

\- Mac Mini / airpods 5 (2nd place)

\-Mac mini (3rd place)

\- Additional prize tracks ($15k+ in prizes including Pocket AI Notetakers): Most likely to scale to millions, People’s Choice, Best Design  

\- All participants get $1k+ in Naive and sponsor credits


Best Mobile Automation · Mobile Prize Track powered by Mobilerun

Allow your agent-run businesses to work on real mobile phones and apps. Publish content, compare ride quotes, place delivery orders, test apps. and much more.  

All teams get 72 hours of access with Android and iOS device minutes and six team seats. iPhones are first come, first served.

Prizes:

1st: 3 cloud iPhone packages ($8,520)
2nd: 2 cloud iPhone packages ($5,760)
3rd: 1 cloud iPhone package ($3,000)

Each runs for 12 months

### Schedule

Nov 7, 2026

11:00 AM: Doors open

11:30 AM: Welcome Note

12:00 PM: Lunch served

1:00 PM: Hacking begins

6:30 PM: Dinner served

Nov 8, 2026

9:00 AM: Breakfast served

11:00 AM: Hacking stops, judging begins

12:00 PM: Lunch served

1:00 PM: Final presentations

1:45 PM: Winner Announcement + Prizes

2:30 PM: Event ends

### Judges & Mentors

Coming soon.

### Rules & Logistics

 Plan to attend both days in San Francisco. Come solo, bring a team, or meet teammates at kickoff.
 Apply through this page. Only approved attendees may attend.
 Attendees must be at least 15. Participants aged 15-17 must have YC's parental consent form signed before the event.
 Teams will present live demos. Judges will focus on how much of the company runs without you.
 Meals, snacks, and non-alcoholic drinks will be provided. Bring your laptop and charger.

### Sponsors

<https://openai.com>: AI research lab and creator of the GPT models.
<https://www.hubspot.com>: CRM platform for marketing, sales, and customer service.
<https://stripe.com>: Payments infrastructure and financial APIs for the internet.
<https://vercel.com>: The platform for deploying and scaling modern web apps.
<https://openrouter.ai>: One API to route requests across hundreds of LLMs from every major provider.
<https://agentmail.to>: Email inbox API that lets AI agents send, receive, and act on emails.
<https://luxor.tech>: GPU compute and AI infrastructure
<https://monid.ai>: OpenRouter for agent tools. Connect your agent to 2,981 tools & APIs with one integration. No subscriptions, just pay as you go.
<https://apify.com>: Web scraping and automation platform with thousands of ready-made data extractors.
<https://mobilerun.ai>: AI agents that operate real Android and iOS phones through natural language.
<https://render.com>: Cloud platform for deploying web services, workers, and databases with zero DevOps.
<https://neon.com>: Serverless Postgres with branching, autoscaling, and scale-to-zero.

Bring a business idea. Build the team that runs it.

candidates.title: VexoHacks - An AI Wearables Hackathon by Vexo
candidates.evidence:
Hosted By
Y Combinator
VexoHacks
Saturday, November 14
San Francisco, CA
Capacity 250
About Event
Join VexoHacks, a one-day AI wearable hackathon by Vexo at Y Combinator in San Francisco. 

Build new ways for people to interact with AI through wearables, voice and real-world experiences—not just another app on a screen.

Developers, designers and hardware builders will come together to prototype and demonstrate AI experiences that fit into everyday life. Vexo bracelets (and more hardware!) will be available for participants who want to build with Vexo voice technology. 

SPONSORS
Google DeepMind, OpenAI, Vexo, ElevenLabs, Minimax, Stripe, Brex, Mastra and more!

PRIZES
Over $15,000 in prizes + a YC final interview!

candidates.title: The Consumer Mobile Hackathon
candidates.evidence:
Hosted By
Y Combinator
Consumer Mobile Hack
Sunday, November 15
San Francisco, CA
Capacity 225
About Event
_Build an app people open every day._

On November 15, 180 builders take over the YC office to build consumer mobile apps in one day.

Consumer apps are having a moment again, and AI has collapsed the time it takes to build one. Come build the app you'd actually want on your home screen, ship it to a real phone by dinner, and demo it to founders and a YC partner who've built consumer products used by millions.

You'll build with Capy, Revyl and Convex, with the Candle team (a YC consumer app with 1M+ users) on the floor all day helping with what makes people come back.

The winning team gets a YC interview. Breakfast, lunch anddinner are on us.

What to build

A consumer app for iOS or Android that someone would want to open again tomorrow. You don't need to ship to the App Store, but it needs to run on a device so you can demo it live.

Tracks

We'll have themed tracks with their own prizes, on top of the overall top 3. Tracks and track prizes will be announced at kickoff, so come with ideas, not code.

Prizes

1st place: a YC interview, plus an iPhone 18 Pro for every team member

2nd place: a MacBook Neo for every team member

3rd place: an Apple Watch for every team member

_Track prizes: announced at kickoff on the day._

Schedule

8:00 AM: Doors open

9:00 AM: Kickoff and lightning talks

10:00 AM: Hacking begins

12:30 PM: Lunch

6:00 PM: Submissions due

6:30 PM: Dinner and chill

7:00 PM: Finalist demos

8:00 PM: Winners announced

9:00 PM: Closing

Rules

Teams of up to 3; solo is welcome.

Start from scratch: all code is written after 10:00 AM.

Must use Capy, Revyl and Convex.

Sponsors

Capy

Revyl

Candle

Convex

(More to be announced soon)
